Heat pumps explained
An air-source heat pump moves heat from outdoor air into a building instead of burning fuel to make it. A refrigerant absorbs heat in the outdoor coil, a compressor raises its temperature, and an indoor coil releases that heat into radiators or air ducts. For every unit of electricity, a well-installed unit delivers three to four units of heat, which is why heat pumps are central to decarbonising homes.
